body:
WHAT
Slash commands (`/help`, `/clear`, `/compact`, ...) are listed once in `SLASH_COMMANDS` in the engine. `/help` renders its text from this list, and the same list plus every installed addon as `/<name>` is sent to the frontend in `session_started.commands` and again in `addons_updated.commands` after an addon install. The frontend's command palette only shows what it received.

WHY
A frontend that derives slash commands itself drifts from what the engine will actually dispatch, and an addon installed mid-session would be invocable but invisible in the palette.

WHERE
engine/core/src/runtime/engine.ts — `const SLASH_COMMANDS`, `renderHelp()`, `announceSession()` (builds `commands`), `addonCommands()`, `emitAddonsUpdated()`, `handleSlash()` (the dispatch switch); engine/protocol/src/types.ts — `interface SlashCommandInfo` (`cmd`, `args`, `desc`, `addon?`), `CoreEvent` variants `session_started` (field `commands`) and `addons_updated` (field `commands?`).

TEST CHECKLIST
1. Every `cmd` in session_started.commands that is not an addon has a matching `case` in handleSlash: send each as slash_command and assert no 'Unknown command' output is produced.
2. The /help output (command_output after slash_command 'help') contains every cmd and desc string from session_started.commands with addon !== true, and nothing else in the built-in section.
3. With an addon named 'review' installed, session_started.commands contains {cmd:'/review', addon:true} and slash_command 'review' is dispatched (no 'Unknown command').
4. Send install_addon with a valid addon file; the resulting addons_updated event carries a `commands` array containing the new '/<name>' entry, and it equals the list a following /clear's session_started would send.
5. Every built-in registry entry has non-empty `cmd` starting with '/' and `desc`, and the list has no duplicate cmd values.
